# fivenines_raid_arrays (Data Source)

The mdadm arrays on this instance: which one is degraded, which member failed, and how far the rebuild got.

READ `status`, NOT THE THREE BOOLEANS. mdstat reports a SET of words and an array is routinely several at once, so `healthy` and `degraded` are BOTH true for the normal shape of a degrading array that is still serving. `status` applies the precedence failed > degraded > healthy; an if/else over the booleans reports a degrading array as fine. The raw set is published as `state` because collapsing it loses "active AND recovering".

The progress percentages are null-means-no-such-operation: a 0 in `rebuild_status_percent` would read as a rebuild stuck at the start, the alarming reading of a perfectly healthy array.

TWO THINGS THIS CANNOT TELL YOU. There is no `stale` field or filter -- the product has no RAID freshness window, so publishing a verdict would invent one; compare `last_synced_at` against `collector.last_reported_at` yourself. And an empty list is ambiguous here in a way it is not elsewhere: RAID ingestion cannot distinguish a collection FAILURE from "this host has no arrays". Do not treat a single empty read as authoritative for a host you know has arrays.

## Example Usage

```terraform
data "fivenines_raid_arrays" "all" {
  instance_id = fivenines_instance.db.id
}

# Read status, not the three booleans: mdstat reports a SET of words, so
# healthy and degraded are both true for a degrading array that still serves.
# status applies the precedence failed > degraded > healthy.
output "arrays_needing_attention" {
  value = [
    for a in data.fivenines_raid_arrays.all.raid_arrays :
    a.device if contains(["failed", "degraded"], a.status)
  ]
}

# The progress percentages are null when no such operation is running -- a 0
# would read as a rebuild stuck at the start.
output "rebuilding" {
  value = {
    for a in data.fivenines_raid_arrays.all.raid_arrays :
    a.device => a.rebuild_status_percent if a.rebuild_status_percent != null
  }
}

# There is no stale field on this collector, so compare last_synced_at against
# the instance's own last check-in yourself.
output "raid_last_reported_at" {
  value = data.fivenines_raid_arrays.all.collector.last_reported_at
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `instance_id` (String) The instance (host) UUID the rows belong to.

### Optional

- `q` (String) Case-insensitive substring match on the device or array name.
- `status` (String) Filter by the precedence verdict (failed > degraded > healthy). One of: `failed`, `degraded`, `healthy`, `unknown`.
- `updated_since` (String) Return only rows whose `updated_at` is at or after this ISO 8601 timestamp. Inclusive, so a row updated in the same instant as the cursor comes back rather than falling through the gap. The ingester touches `updated_at` on every agent tick, so this is a freshness filter rather than a change feed, and there are no tombstones: a row the agent stops reporting is deleted.

### Read-Only

- `collector` (Attributes) Why the row list looks the way it does. Read this before treating an empty list as a clean bill of health: `[]` alone cannot distinguish "this host genuinely runs none" from "the collector is switched off" (which deletes the rows) or "this agent is too old to report them". (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--collector))
- `raid_arrays` (Attributes List) The rows the collector reported. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--raid_arrays))

<a id="nestedatt--collector"></a>
### Nested Schema for `collector`

Read-Only:

- `blocked_reason` (String) The agent's own explanation, where it sent one. Null otherwise.
- `enabled` (Boolean) Whether the operator has this collector switched on for the instance. Switching it off deletes the rows, so `false` fully explains an empty list.
- `last_reported_at` (String) The instance's last agent check-in -- not this collector's. It separates "this collector went quiet" (rows stale, instance reporting) from "the whole agent went quiet" (both). Per-row freshness is each row's `last_synced_at`.
- `name` (String) The collector these rows come from.
- `pending` (Boolean) Enabled, and the agent knows the feature, but the capability is not satisfied yet (missing binary, missing permission). The rows are legitimately absent and may appear on a later tick.
- `supported` (Boolean) Whether this agent can collect these rows -- its own capability verdict where it reports one, its version otherwise. `false` alongside `enabled` means the instance was asked for something it cannot deliver. Read it as "the agent has not said it cannot": the config-driven collectors (haproxy, rabbitmq, php_fpm, wireguard) have no version floor, so an agent predating one still reports `true` with an empty list.
- `unavailable_reason` (String) Why `supported` is false: `host_lacks_feature` (the agent probed and reported it cannot) or `agent_outdated` (the agent predates the release that collects these rows). Null when supported.


<a id="nestedatt--raid_arrays"></a>
### Nested Schema for `raid_arrays`

Read-Only:

- `active_devices` (Number) Devices mdadm counts as active. Null when not reported, not 0.
- `array_size` (String) mdadm's human string. The numeric twin is `array_size_num`.
- `array_size_num` (Number) Bytes.
- `check_status` (String) Null unless a scrub/check is in flight.
- `check_status_percent` (Number) Percent complete. Null means no check is running -- see `resync_status_percent`.
- `chunk_size` (String) Chunk size as mdadm printed it, e.g. `512K`. Null when not reported.
- `chunk_size_num` (Number) Chunk size in bytes, parsed from `chunk_size`. Null when unparsed or not reported.
- `component_devices` (List of String) The member block devices. This is how you find the disk to replace, and the reason this row beats the metric series.
- `consistency_policy` (String) mdadm's consistency policy for the array, e.g. `bitmap`. Null when not reported.
- `created_at` (String) When this row was first recorded. This is when the agent first happened to report it, not anything an operator would recognize.
- `creation_time` (String) When mdadm reports the array was created. Null when not reported.
- `degraded` (Boolean) The state set contains "degraded". See `healthy`.
- `device` (String) The kernel device, and the identity (the upsert key is host + device).
- `events` (String) mdadm's event counter as printed. Null when not reported.
- `events_num` (Number) mdadm's event counter, parsed. Null when unparsed or not reported.
- `failed` (Boolean) The state set contains "failed". See `healthy`.
- `failed_devices` (Number) Devices mdadm counts as failed. **Null means not reported, never "none failed".**
- `healthy` (Boolean) The state set contains "active" or "clean". DOES NOT PARTITION with the two below: a degraded array that is still serving reads `healthy: true` AND `degraded: true`. An if/else over these three reports a degrading array as fine -- read `status` instead.
- `host_id` (String) The instance (host) UUID this row belongs to.
- `id` (Number) Row identifier.
- `last_synced_at` (String) When the agent last reported this array. THERE IS NO `stale` FIELD ON THIS COLLECTOR -- the product has no RAID freshness window anywhere, so publishing a verdict here would invent one. Compare this against `collector.last_reported_at` yourself if you need a freshness call.
- `mdadm_version` (String) The mdadm metadata version, e.g. `1.2`. Null when not reported.
- `name` (String) mdadm's own array name, which is NOT the device and is often blank.
- `persistence` (String) mdadm's superblock persistence line. Null when not reported.
- `physical_disks` (Number) How many physical disks mdadm attributes to the array.
- `preferred_minor` (Number) The array's preferred minor device number. Null when not reported.
- `raid_level` (String) The array's RAID level, e.g. `raid1`. Null when mdadm did not report it.
- `rebuild_status` (String) Null unless a rebuild is in flight.
- `rebuild_status_percent` (Number) Percent complete. Null means no rebuild is running -- see `resync_status_percent`.
- `resync_status` (String) Null unless a resync is in flight.
- `resync_status_percent` (Number) Percent complete. NULL MEANS NO RESYNC IS RUNNING -- a 0 would read as a resync stuck at the start.
- `spare_devices` (Number) Devices mdadm counts as spares. Null when not reported, not 0.
- `state` (List of String) The raw /proc/mdstat word SET, verbatim. An array really can be several at once ("active" AND "degraded"), which is why this is a list and why collapsing it loses information -- a degrading array that is still serving is a different situation from one that is not.
- `status` (String) The collapsed verdict, with precedence failed > degraded > healthy. THIS IS THE FIELD TO BRANCH ON. `unknown` means the state set matched none of them, not that the array is fine. One of: `failed`, `degraded`, `healthy`, `unknown`.
- `total_devices` (Number) Devices mdadm counts in the array. Null when not reported, not 0.
- `update_time` (String) When mdadm last updated the array superblock. Null when not reported.
- `updated_at` (String) When this row was last written. The ingester touches it on every agent tick, so it is a freshness stamp rather than a change feed.
- `used_dev_size` (String) Per-device size as mdadm printed it. Null when not reported.
- `used_dev_size_num` (Number) Per-device size in bytes, parsed from `used_dev_size`. Null when unparsed or not reported.
- `uuid` (String) The mdadm array UUID, stable across a device renumbering.
- `version` (String) The mdadm superblock version.
- `working_devices` (Number) Devices mdadm counts as working. Null when not reported, not 0.
